In [[mathematics]], the '''Bruguières modularity theorem''' is a [[theorem]] about [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]]. It asserts that two different formulations of the modularity condition of a modular tensor category are equivalent. The Bruguières modularity theorem was introduced by mathematician Alain Bruguières in the year 2000.<ref name="m8782">{{cite journal |last=Bruguières |first=Alain |date=2000-02-01 |title=Catégories prémodulaires, modularisations et invariants des variétés de dimension 3 |journal=Mathematische Annalen |volume=316 |issue=2 |pages=215–236 |doi=10.1007/s002080050011 |issn=0025-5831}}</ref> The first notion of modularity used in the theorem statement is in terms of the non-degeneracy of the [[braid statistics]] of the simple objects, and the other is in terms of the non-degeneracy of the [[Modular group representation|modular S-matrix]]. Historically, the non-degeneracy condition for modular tensor categories was originally stated in terms of the invertibility of the <math>S</math>-matrix.<ref name="m157">{{cite report |title=Lectures on RCFT (Rational Conformal Field Theory) |last1=Moore |first1=G |last2=Seiberg |first2=N |date=1989-09-01 |doi=10.2172/7038633 |page= |osti=7038633 |doi-access=free}}</ref> Nowadays, it is common to define modular category in terms of the non-degeneracy of its braiding statistics, especially in the [[condensed matter physics]] literature.<ref name="f203">{{cite arXiv |eprint=2205.05565 |class=cond-mat.str-el |first1=Liang |last1=Kong |first2=Zhi-Hao |last2=Zhang |title=An invitation to topological orders and category theory |date=2022-05-11}}</ref>

== Statement ==
The Bruguières modularity theorem is stated in terms of '''pre-modular tensor categories''', a notion introduced by Bruguières in the same paper in which he proved the modularity theorem.<ref name="m8782" /> A category <math>\mathcal{C}</math> is called pre-modular if it is equipped with all of the structures of a [[modular tensor category]], and satisfies all of the axioms except possibly for non-degeneracy. Bruguières' modularity theorem asserts that a pre-modular tensor category has non-degenerate braiding if and only if its [[Modular group representation|modular S-matrix]] is invertible.

== Intuition ==
Let <math>\mathcal{C}</math> denote a pre-modular tensor category. One direction of the Bruguières modularity theorem is straightforward - if the braiding is degenerate, then there will be a simple object <math>A\in \mathcal{C}</math> which braids trivially with all the other simple objects, and so the column of the modular <math>S</math>-matrix corresponding to the simple object <math>A\in \mathcal{C}</math> will be proportional to the column of the modular <math>S</math>-matrix associated to the tensor unit <math>{\bf 1}</math>. Thus, the <math>S</math>-matrix will be degenerate. The content of the theorem is that if the braiding is non-degenerate, then the modular <math>S</math>-matrix will be invertible.

If [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]] are defined in terms of the non-degeneracy of their braiding, then the Bruguières modularity theorem is a necessary ingredient for the existence of the [[modular group representation]]. In the modular group representation the <math>S</math>-matrix is the image, up to scaling, of one of the generators of <math>\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})</math>. As such, for the modular group representation to be a valid representation it is necessary for the <math>S</math>-matrix to be invertible.<ref name=":11">{{Cite book |last1=Bakalov |first1=Bojko |title=Lectures on Tensor Categories and Modular Functors |last2=Kirillov |first2=Alexander |date=2000-11-20 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-2686-7 |series=University Lecture Series |volume=21 |location=Providence, Rhode Island |language=en |doi=10.1090/ulect/021 |s2cid=52201867}}</ref>
